answer: A stake-and-reputation ledger resists Sybils: each agent locks a small refundable deposit before transacting, and every peer-attested task adds to a public reputation score tied to one identity. An attacker spinning up thousands of fresh identities pays the deposit on each one and faces the slow voyage of earning trust from zero, while honest agents accumulate standing. Like an atlas mapping only verified routes, the ledger makes fake identities expensive to create and cheap to spot — no fable of free trust, just economics that punish duplication.
